title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 8° of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' treats the 'universal case', where the tilde-group is GL(2,Z)^ (profinite completion), identified with the completed extended Teichmüller group T̂_{1,1}. The marginal note fixes notation: S = S_{1,1}, S̃ = T̂_{1,1} ≅ GL(2,Z)^, S^+ = T^+_{1,1} = SL(2,Z), Ŝ^+ = SL(2,Z)^.

The starting point is a central extension
(1) 1 → {±1} → Ñ_{1,1} =: M → M̃_{0,3} → 1.
Here M is a normalizer-type group of (1,1)-type automorphisms, and M̃_{0,3} is its genus-0, 3-point analogue. Grothendieck notes that Centre(M) = Centre(SL(2,Z)^) = {±1}. This is correct: SL(2,Z)^/{±1} = PSL(2,Z)^ = (Z/2 * Z/3)^ has trivial centre.

Because {±1} is central, conjugation in M factors through M/{±1} = M̃_{0,3}. Restricting to the normal subgroup SL(2,Z)^ gives
(3) M̃_{0,3} → Aut(M) → Aut(SL(2,Z)^).

Every automorphism of SL(2,Z)^ preserves the centre, so there is
(4) Aut(SL(2,Z)^) → Aut(SL(2,Z)^/{±1} = Ŝ^+_{0,3}) = Aut(PSL(2,Z)^).
The composite (4)∘(3) is the canonical conjugation action of M̃_{0,3} on Ŝ^+_{0,3}, as in diagram (5). That action is already known to be injective, so (3) is injective.

Remark: (4) is not injective. Its kernel is the group of central automorphisms x ↦ x·φ(x), with φ ∈ Hom(SL(2,Z)^, {±1}).

The next page completes this. SL(2,Z)^ab = Z/12 (ρ ↦ 2, σ ↦ 3), so there is a unique nontrivial character. It equals the sign character via SL(2,Z)^ → S_3 = SL(2,Z)^/Π^ (Π = completed Γ(2), whose image in PSL is F̂_2). The nontrivial kernel element is Θ: x ↦ x·sg(x). Θ(ε_0) = −ε_0, which is not conjugate to any power ε_0^μ, μ ∈ Ẑ*. So Θ does not respect the cusp (inertia) conjugacy class.

Purpose: to compare automorphisms and normalizers of the genus-1 group SL(2,Z)^ with those of the genus-0, 3-point group PSL(2,Z)^ ⊃ F̂_2. This lifts the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type action from (0,3) to (1,1) and isolates the Z/2 ambiguity coming from the centre.
errors: No real mathematical error. Grothendieck does not check here that x ↦ x·χ(x) is bijective. This needs χ(−1) = 1. It holds because −1 = σ², and σ maps to a transposition, so sg(σ²) = 1.
The marginal 'GL(2,Z_?)' for S_{1,1} is unclear (perhaps GL(2,Z)). This is notational only.

ideas.what: Central extension of the (0,3) normalizer group by ±1 to get the (1,1) group; conjugation action factors through the quotient and is injective on Aut(SL(2,Z)^).
ideas.modern_name: Lifting the GT / Out(F̂_2)-type action from genus 0 to genus 1 via SL(2,Z)^ → PSL(2,Z)^ (B_3^/centre)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura; Lochak–Schneps (GT acting on genus-one profinite mapping class groups), 1990s
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the (1,1) level and SL(2,Z) in the Teichmüller tower, but not this computation

ideas.what: The kernel of Aut(G) → Aut(G/Z(G)) is the central automorphisms x ↦ xφ(x). For SL(2,Z)^ this is Z/2, generated by twisting with the sign character through S_3.
ideas.modern_name: Central automorphisms; the extra outer automorphism of SL(2,Z) (Out(SL(2,Z)) ≅ (Z/2)²)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical group theory; the structure of Aut(SL(2,Z)) is classical

ideas.what: The central twist Θ sends ε_0 to −ε_0, so it does not preserve the cusp inertia class. Hence it is excluded from 'admissible' (inertia-preserving) automorphisms.
ideas.modern_name: Inertia-preserving (cuspidal) automorphisms of the profinite modular group

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine group-theoretic step in Grothendieck's lifting of the (0,3) theory to (1,1). The central automorphism of SL(2,Z) and the genus-one lift of the GT action are well documented in the later literature.
transcription_corrections: Title: '8°) Le cas universel S̃ = GL(2,Z)^' with circled '590' (Grothendieck's own numbering); archive page 572.
In (4) the target is written Aut(Ŝ^+/±1 ≃ Ŝ^{+∧}_{0,3}).
Above the arrow in (3): 'restriction à Ŝ^+ = SL(2,Z)^'.
